Package frc.robot.subsystems

Interface Subsystem

All Superinterfaces:
edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Subsystem
All Known Implementing Classes:
AbstractArmSubsystem, AbstractElevatorSubsystem, ArmSubsystem, ElevatorSubsystem, SimArmSubsystem, SimElevatorSubsystem, SubsystemBase
public interface Subsystem extends edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Subsystem
The contract every mechanism in this library exposes to robot code.

This extends WPILib's Subsystem, so a mechanism here is a first-class subsystem in the command-based framework: it can be required by a Command, it participates in loop timing, and it appears in the scheduler. Extending rather than wrapping is deliberate — a library that defined its own parallel concept of a subsystem would force every team to write adapters.

The extra methods beyond WPILib's interface are the three things a robot has to be able to ask of any mechanism, plus the metadata an Operator Interface needs.

For users of this library

Hold mechanisms by interface, not implementation: 


 ArmSubsystem arm = new ArmSubsystem(new TalonFXArmIO(ArmHardware.CAN_ID), ArmHardware.CONSTANTS);
 arm.setTargetAngle(Rotation2d.fromRotations(0.25));

 for (Subsystem mechanism : List.of(arm, elevator)) {
   mechanism.periodic();
 }

For implementers of this library

Extend SubsystemBase, which supplies the loop bookkeeping and goal tracking. Behaviour shared between a real and a simulated variant belongs in the abstract class between the two, not here.

  • Method Details

    • periodic

      default void periodic()
      Runs one iteration of the mechanism's control loop.

      Called once per robot loop. Implementations read inputs, compute an output, and apply it to their IO. This must not block: it runs on a fixed 20 ms budget, and overrunning it starves the rest of the robot.

      Implementations must be safe to call in a test process with no hardware attached.

      Specified by:
      periodic in interface edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.Subsystem

    • stop

      void stop()
      Drops every output to a safe state.

      Called when the robot is disabled and during shutdown. This is a safety-critical path: it must not throw, must not depend on inputs being healthy, and must leave the mechanism where it will not move on its own once re-enabled.

    • atGoal

      boolean atGoal()
      Returns whether the mechanism has reached the goal it was most recently commanded to.

      Used by robot code to sequence mechanisms and by tests to assert a command completed. A mechanism with no active goal reports true.

      Returns:
      true if the mechanism is at its goal and has nothing left to do

    • isReal

      boolean isReal()
      Returns whether this mechanism is driving real hardware.

      Callers use this to skip hardware-only work, and tests use it to skip assertions that only make sense against real motors. A simulated implementation returns false.

      Returns:
      true for real hardware, false for a simulated implementation

    • getName

      Returns a stable, human-readable name for this mechanism.

      Used for logging, dashboards, and diagnostics. It should be unique across the robot.
